note: The founders on record (Karouma's 78s, Sarour) and then the haqiba singers of Radio Omdurman's long afterlife (Badi Mohamed al-Tayeb, Mirghani al-Ma'mun and Ahmed Hassan Gumaa, Mubarak Hassan Barakat, Abdel Aziz Mohamed Daoud, Kamal Tarbas), mostly from the Nile Melodies Archive 'Haqibat al-Fann' reissues, ending with two recent haqiba albums by Insaf Fathi and Asim Albanna. Archive reissues carry no recording year, so their years are left null.

size.basis: A judgement made before collecting, not a count. Haqiba is a closed 1920s–1940s song repertoire by a few dozen Omdurman poets and singers (Khalil Farah, Abu Salah, Sayed Abdel Aziz, Obeid Abdel Rahman; singers Wad El Faki, Sarour, Karouma, Al-Amin Burhan), first on Cairo-made 78s in the 1930s and then kept alive on Radio Omdurman's Hageebat al-Fann programme and by later singers and ensembles re-recording the same few hundred songs. Low allows for a few hundred songs times few surviving versions; high counts the many re-recordings by later Sudanese singers and haqiba ensembles on cassette, radio and online. An insider's essential list is about 30 songs. Pages read afterwards fit this: Karouma alone wrote several hundred songs, Mubarak Hassan Barakat was said to know 1000 haqiba songs and recorded over 600, and the Nile Melodies Archive's 2024 'Haqibat al-Fann' series re-issues the same songs by many singers.
